remainingEvidence: §3.5 fixes the shape by composition — custody is the (SecretRef, consumer, endpoint) triple a Tenant-owned consumer's own record carries, the resolution seam is §4.5's credential-isolation seam, and denial is an ordinary failed AttemptReceipt (§7.4) — so nothing about this atom is still a spec ambiguity

The §4.5 SHOULD does not weaken the rule and is not what blocks the atom: §3.5's requirement is conditional on resolving at all, so any seam that resolves a SecretRef MUST check custody first. What blocks it is that no such seam exists to check anything. P11-ENVIRONMENT-CREDENTIAL-SEAM is verified against the *shape* of the seam only (src/facets/environment/facet.ts#EnvironmentFacet, evidenced by a test that credential isolation passes only a bound capability and content references); EnvironmentCredentialPort.forward and EnvironmentCredentialIsolationProxy are both abstract with no implementation anywhere in the tree, and SecretRef (src/core/secret-ref.ts) is a self-contained value type with no custody association at all

Verifying this atom needs three pieces that do not exist: a custody association durably carried by a consumer record and validating `source` against the exact canonical TenantId; one concrete resolution seam that consults it before forwarding and fails rather than degrading on a mismatched or unrecorded pair; and a mediated externalSend path recording that failure as an ordinary failed AttemptReceipt. A custody type no seam consults would be evidence for nothing, so the enforcement point is the load-bearing part

Ownership is a live constraint on the flip: the atom is filed under W4 (src/definition/**) while the only place a custody check can bind is a concrete EnvironmentCredentialPort in W3/W8 and the denial receipt is W6. Under the single-owner evidence rule the owner must either accept cross-wave sourcing for this atom or place the custody record and its check in the definition plane with the seam calling into it

remainingEvidence: The declaration half is built and discrimination-tested. PlacementPolicy carries `backings` (src/definition/placement.ts#AuthoredCodeBackingPolicy), a partial map from the closed §4.7 consumer set to an opaque AuthoredCodeBackingId, read through PlacementPolicy.backingFor(consumer, profileDefault); an unmapped consumer takes the substrate profile's declared default and never another offered backing. test/definition/authored-code-backing.test.ts covers it under this atom's id, and four mutations — ignoring the declaration, sending an unmapped consumer to a declared backing, dropping the mapping on encode, and opening the consumer set — each break a cited test.

Both backings §10.2 names are now implemented (packages/agent-core-cloudflare/src/authored-code.ts), so the atom's second conjunct — every offered backing preserves identical `dynamic` authority semantics — finally has subjects. Worker Loader discharges it: the isolate is loaded with `globalOutbound: null`, `disallow_importable_env`, and an `env` holding one entrypoint stub per delegated Binding and nothing else, all three exercised against real workerd in the cloudflare lane.

The dispatch-namespace backing does not discharge it. It resolves a script deployed earlier, whose outbound posture is a property of that deployment and of the namespace binding's own `outbound` configuration — neither visible nor settable from the adapter at call time — so nothing in the tree demonstrates zero ambient egress for it. §4.7 requires each backing to demonstrate the invariant independently, 'never by comparison against another backing', so Worker Loader's evidence cannot stand for it.

C13-PLACEMENT-DYNAMIC-NO-EGRESS is therefore declared as a prerequisite rather than left implicit: this atom's second conjunct is discharged through it, and it is planned. Verifying this atom needs that atom's substrate-neutral domain-construction seam to cover pre-deployed code as well as loaded code, and needs the ownership question it already records to be answered — the enforcement points are W8's, and a W4-owned atom cannot cite a cloudflare/ test.

The rule is enforced at the substrate (SPEC §1.5: an outbound policy code can reach around is advice), but W4's definition plane holds only the dynamic mode token; the sole enforcement point is globalOutbound: null in the W8 Cloudflare loader, which W4 cannot cite

Needs a substrate-neutral domain-construction seam in the definition plane whose contract is no-ambient-egress with destinations only as passed Bindings, implemented by the Cloudflare loader and a local reference, before W4-citable evidence exists
Adversarial evidence: loaded code attempting an outbound connection with no Binding must be denied by the substrate, not by a policy check inside the domain
